subject: Next step: Dedicated capacity sizing call for PayLane
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@paylane.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lina Torres <lina@paylane.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — PayLane x Redwood

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — it was really helpful to see the latency and cost controls you outlined. Lina and I took notes and we feel comfortable moving to a sizing session to align on dedicated capacity. Our goals for the upcoming call:

- Walk through PayLane's sustained query profile and peaks
- Establish target P95 latency for synchronous flows (card auth, fraud checks)
- Validate batch/embedding throughput for nightly reconciliation jobs
- Confirm network/VPC and data retention constraints for Private/Dedicated options

Would you and whoever from your engineering/ops team can join be available next week? We can do a 60-minute technical sizing call where we share traffic samples. Lina attached a short CSV with the last 24 hours of traffic and a proposed .ics for the two windows we can hold.

Attached: current-traffic-snapshot.csv, proposed-slots.ics

Preferred windows (Pacific): Wed 9/22 10:00–11:00 or Thu 9/23 14:00–15:00. If neither works, send a few other options or a Calendly link and we'll pick.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Patel
VP Product, PayLane

---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@paylane.com>
Cc: Lina Torres <lina@paylane.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — PayLane x Redwood

Samir — appreciated the follow-up and the traffic snapshot. Glad the demo was useful.

We can do the sizing call and will treat it as the dedicated-capacity intake: we'll want to capture peak QPS, typical sequence lengths, and the P95 latency targets for each critical path. Quick ask before we lock a slot: can you confirm roughly the following so we come prepared?

- Peak sustained QPS (or QPS range) during business hours
- Burst QPS (short spikes) and typical duration
- Average and 95th percentile request lengths (in tokens/characters) for auth & reconciliation flows
- Whether you expect large batch embedding runs (rough size of daily job in requests/min)
- Any hard P95 latency target (e.g., <= 150ms) or max tolerated latency

Proposed next steps:
1) We take Thu 9/23 14:00–15:00 PT as primary (I'll also add a 9/22 10:00–11:00 PT backup on my side).
2) I'll include Grace (solutions lead) and Evelyn (capacity engineer) on the sizing call — they'll drive the workload intake.
3) Please upload a short CSV with a one-week sample if you can (headers: timestamp, endpoint, latency_ms, payload_size_bytes). If not, the 24h snapshot you attached is fine for an initial estimate.
4) We'll send a short intake worksheet (paylane-sizing-checklist.pdf) before the call.

Calendly: https://calendly.com/redwood-inference/60min — happy to lock whichever slot is easiest for you.

I'll tentatively put Thu 9/23 14:00–15:00 PT on our calendars and send an invite once you confirm.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

---
From: Lina Torres <lina@paylane.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@paylane.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — PayLane x Redwood

Karthik / Grace — thanks for the quick turnaround. Confirming Thu 9/23 14:00–15:00 PT works for Samir and me. We uploaded a one-week sample to the spreadsheet and included a short notes column explaining which endpoints are latency-sensitive. I re-attached the 24h CSV in case it helps.

Quick answers to your intake questions:
- Typical business-hour sustained QPS: 45–70
- Burst QPS: up to ~220 for short windows (<= 3m) during peak campaigns
- Avg request token-equivalent: ~120 tokens for auth flows; reconciliation batch items are very small per-request but run in large numbers overnight
- Expected daily batch embedding job: ~180k items, executed as parallelized jobs over off-peak windows
- Target P95 for auth: <= 200ms; for fraud-checking path we'd like <= 350ms if possible

We'll attach current-traffic-snapshot.csv to the calendar invite. See you on Thu.

Cheers,
Lina Torres
Head of Platform Engineering, PayLane

Attachments: current-traffic-snapshot.csv

---
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 11:17:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap — PayLane x Redwood (sizing call confirmed)

Karthik / Evelyn — forwarding the confirmation from PayLane. They locked Thu 9/23 14:00–15:00 PT and included the one-week sample & summary. Evelyn, can you join as the capacity engineer and prepare our initial cost/throughput model? Key prep items:

- Run the quick intake against the spreadsheet: estimate GPU footprint for sustained 70 QPS at 120 token avg and ~220 burst handling with fallback policy
- Prepare two recommended configurations (cost-optimized and latency-optimized) with rough monthly unit economics
- Bring the sample mutual action plan template so we can capture post-call deliverables (MOP: scoped deliverables, SLA target, next steps to provision a reserved pool)

I'll create the calendar invite and attach paylane-sizing-checklist.pdf and the PayLane CSV that Lina provided. If you want to pair with someone from runtime, let me know — otherwise we'll handle initial sizing and follow with an ops deep-dive if needed.

Thanks — Grace
Grace O'Connor
Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
